title.zh: 卷八十二 列傳第三十二: 許敬宗 李義府
title.en: Volume 82 Biographies 32: Xu Jingzong, Li Yifu
title.raw: 卷八十二 列傳第三十二: 許敬宗 李義府 Volume 82 Biographies 32: Xu Jingzong, Li Yifu

sentences.zh: 許敬宗

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong

sentences.zh: 許敬宗，杭州新城人，隋禮部侍郎善心子也。

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong was a native of Xincheng in Hangzhou, the son of Shanzin, Vice Minister of Rites under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong came from Xincheng in Hangzhou; he was the son of Shanzin, who had served the Sui as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 其先自高陽南渡，世仕江左。

translations.literal: His forebears had crossed south from Gaoyang, and for generations the family had served in the Jiangzuo region.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had moved south from Gaoyang and held office in the lower Yangzi region for generations.

sentences.zh: 敬宗幼善屬文，舉秀才，授淮陽郡司法書佐，俄直謁者台，奏通事舍人事。

translations.literal: Jingzong from youth was skilled at literary composition; he passed the Xiucai examination and was appointed judicial clerk of Huaiyang commandery; soon he served in the Directorate of Audiences and was recommended for the post of Master of Ceremonies for diplomatic reception.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Jingzong showed a gift for writing. After passing the provincial examination he became a judicial clerk in Huaiyang commandery, then soon joined the Directorate of Audiences and was posted as Master of Ceremonies for foreign envoys.

sentences.zh: 江都之難，善心為宇文化及所害。

translations.literal: At the disaster at Jiangdu, Shanzin was killed by Yuwen Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiangdu coup Shanzin was killed by Yuwen Huaji.

sentences.zh: 敬宗流轉，投於李密，密以為元帥府記室，與魏徵同為管記。

translations.literal: Jingzong wandered about and went over to Li Mi, who made him secretary of the marshal's headquarters, serving jointly with Wei Zheng as chief recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong drifted through the turmoil until he joined Li Mi, who appointed him secretary on his staff alongside Wei Zheng as co-recorder.

sentences.zh: 武德初，赤牒擬漣州別駕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, a red document proposed him as Assistant Administrator of Lian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era a formal nomination slated him for assistant administrator of Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞其名，召補秦府學士。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong heard his name and summoned him to fill a post as academician of the Prince of Qin's household.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard of him he summoned him as a literary adviser to the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 貞觀八年，累除著作郎，兼修國史，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted to Gentleman of the Palace Library, concurrently compiling the national history, and was transferred to Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 8 he rose to Gentleman of the Palace Library while also compiling the national history, then was promoted to Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十年，文德皇后崩，百官縗絰。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Empress Wende died, and all officials wore hemp mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Empress Wende died, and the entire bureaucracy went into hemp mourning.

sentences.zh: 率更令歐陽詢狀貌醜異，眾或指之，敬宗見而大笑，為御史所劾，左授洪州都督府司馬。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xun, Director of the Imperial Workshops, had an ugly and strange appearance; the crowd sometimes pointed at him, and when Jingzong saw this he burst into loud laughter. He was impeached by the censorate and demoted to military adjutant of the Hongzhou area command.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xun, Director of the Imperial Workshops, had a grotesque appearance, and people in the crowd would point at him. Jingzong saw this and laughed aloud. The censors impeached him, and he was demoted to military adjutant at the Hongzhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中，兼修國史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Attendant Censor and concurrently compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in turn to Attendant Censor while continuing to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 十七年，以修《武德》、《貞觀實錄》成，封高陽縣男，賜物八百段，權檢校黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, because the compilation of the Veritable Records of Wude and Zhenguan was completed, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyang county, granted eight hundred rolls of goods, and given acting authority as Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, when the Veritable Records of the Wude and Zhenguan reigns were finished, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyang, given eight hundred rolls of goods, and appointed acting Vice Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 高宗在春宮，遷太子右庶子。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was in the Eastern Palace, Jingzong was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozong was still crown prince, Jingzong was made Right Vice Director of his household.

sentences.zh: 十九年，太宗親伐高麗，皇太子定州監國，敬宗與高士廉等共知機要。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Emperor Taizong personally campaigned against Goguryeo; the crown prince supervised the state at Dingzhou, and Jingzong together with Gao Shilian and others jointly handled confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Taizong led the campaign against Goguryeo in person. The crown prince remained at Dingzhou to oversee the realm, and Jingzong joined Gao Shilian and others in managing state secrets.

sentences.zh: 中書令岑文本卒於行所，令敬宗以本官檢校中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Chief Minister of the Secretariat Cen Wuben died on campaign, and Jingzong was ordered to act as Vice Director of the Secretariat while retaining his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Cen Wuben died on campaign, and Jingzong was ordered to serve as acting Vice Director of the Secretariat while keeping his existing post.

sentences.zh: 太宗大破遼賊於駐蹕山，敬宗立於馬前受旨草詔書，詞彩甚麗，深見嗟賞。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong inflicted a great defeat on the Liaodong enemy at Mount Zhubi; Jingzong stood before his horse to receive orders and draft the edict—the diction was very splendid, and he was deeply admired.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong won a great victory over the Liaodong forces at Mount Zhubi. Jingzong stood at his horse's head to take dictation and draft the edict; the prose was so fine that the emperor greatly praised him.

sentences.zh: 先是，庶人承乾廢黜，宮僚多被除削，久未收敘。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the commoner Chengqian was deposed, many palace officials had been dismissed and stripped of rank, and for a long time had not been restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the deposed heir Chengqian was cast aside, many of his household officials had been dismissed and stripped of rank, and for years had not been reappointed.

sentences.zh: 敬宗上表曰：「臣聞先王慎罰，務在於恤刑，往哲寬仁，義在於宥過。

translations.literal: Jingzong submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that the ancient kings were cautious in punishment and strove to show compassion in penal affairs; the sages of old were lenient and humane, and their principle lay in pardoning offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong submitted a memorial: "I have heard that the ancient kings were cautious in imposing punishment and sought to temper the law with mercy, and that the sages of old were lenient and humane because their purpose was to forgive faults.

sentences.zh: 聖人之道，莫尚於茲。

translations.literal: In the way of the sage, nothing is more exalted than this.
translations.idiomatic: In the way of the sage, nothing ranks higher than this.

sentences.zh: 竊見廢官，五品以上，除名棄斥，頗歷歲時。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed that dismissed officials of the fifth rank and above, whose names were struck from the rolls and who were cast out, have already passed through many years.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that officials of the fifth rank and above who were dismissed when Chengqian fell—struck from the rolls and cast out—have already waited many years.

sentences.zh: 但庶人疇昔之年，身處不疑之地，苞藏悖逆，陰結宰臣，所預奸謀，多連宗戚。

translations.literal: Yet in years past the commoner, while in a position free from suspicion, harbored rebellion, secretly joined with chief ministers, and in the treacherous plots in which he took part many were connected by kinship to the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in those years the deposed heir, though he stood in a position of unquestioned trust, harbored treason, secretly colluded with chief ministers, and drew many kinsmen of the imperial house into his plots.

sentences.zh: 禍生慮表，非可防萌，宮內官僚，迥無關預。

translations.literal: Disaster arose beyond what could be foreseen and could not be prevented at the first sprout; the palace officials had no connection with it whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: The disaster arose beyond what anyone could foresee and could not be stopped at the first sign; the palace staff had nothing to do with it at all.

sentences.zh: 今乃投鼠及器，孰謂無冤？

translations.literal: Now you strike at the rat and damage the vessel—who would say there is no injustice?
translations.idiomatic: Now you strike at the rat and break the vessel beside it—who can say there is no injustice?

sentences.zh: 焚山毀玉，稍同遷怒。

translations.literal: To burn the mountain and destroy the jade is much like venting anger on the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: To burn the mountain and ruin the jade within is much like punishing the innocent in a fit of anger.

sentences.zh: 伏尋先典，例有可原。

translations.literal: Your servant has examined the ancient statutes, and there are precedents for pardon.
translations.idiomatic: When I consult the ancient statutes, I find precedents for pardon.

sentences.zh: 昔吳國陪臣，則爰絲不坐於劉濞；

translations.literal: In olden times, among the attendant ministers of the state of Wu, Yuan Si was not punished for Liu Pi's crime;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Yuan Si, a minister of Wu, was not punished for Liu Pi's rebellion;

sentences.zh: 昌邑中尉，則王吉免緣於海昏。

translations.literal: the commandant of Changyi, Wang Ji, was spared because of the Marquis of Haihun.
translations.idiomatic: and Wang Ji, commandant of Changyi, was spared when the Marquis of Haihun was deposed.

sentences.zh: 譬諸欒布，乃策名於彭越；

translations.literal: To compare with Luan Bu, he entered service under Peng Yue;
translations.idiomatic: Luan Bu entered Peng Yue's service;

sentences.zh: 比乎田叔，亦委質於張敖。

translations.literal: and like Tian Shu, he pledged himself to Zhang Ao.
translations.idiomatic: and Tian Shu pledged himself to Zhang Ao—

sentences.zh: 主以凶逆，陷其誅夷；

translations.literal: their lords because of treason fell into execution and extermination;
translations.idiomatic: yet when their lords were executed for treason,

sentences.zh: 臣以賢良，荷彼收擢。

translations.literal: the ministers because of worth were favored with recruitment and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: the ministers themselves, for their worth, were taken up and promoted.

sentences.zh: 歷觀往代，此類尤多。

translations.literal: Surveying past ages, cases of this kind are especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back through the ages, such cases are especially common.

sentences.zh: 近者有隋，又遵斯義。

translations.literal: In recent times the Sui again followed this principle.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui, in our own recent past, followed the same principle.

sentences.zh: 楊勇之廢，罪止加於佞人，李綱之徒，皆不預於刑網。

translations.literal: When Yang Yong was deposed, guilt fell only on the flatterers; men such as Li Gang were none of them caught in the penal net.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yong was deposed, only the flatterers were punished; men such as Li Gang were never caught in the penal net.

sentences.zh: 古今裁其折衷，史籍稱為美談。

translations.literal: Ancient and modern judged the mean between extremes, and the historical records praise this as a fine story.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient and modern historians have praised such balanced judgments as a fine example.

sentences.zh: 而今張玄素、令狐德棻、趙弘智、裴宣機、蕭鈞等，並砥節勵操，有雅望於當朝；

translations.literal: Yet now Zhang Xuansu, Linghu Defen, Zhao Hongzhi, Pei Xuanji, Xiao Jun, and others all sharpen their integrity and strengthen their conduct, and enjoy refined repute at court;
translations.idiomatic: Yet today Zhang Xuansu, Linghu Defen, Zhao Hongzhi, Pei Xuanji, Xiao Jun, and others have all polished their integrity and enjoy high repute at court;

sentences.zh: 經明行修，播令名於天下。

translations.literal: they are versed in the classics and cultivated in conduct, and spread a fine name throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: they are learned in the classics and exemplary in conduct, and their good names are known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 或以直言而遭箠撲，或以忤意而見猜嫌，一概雷同，並罹天憲，恐於王道，傷在未弘。

translations.literal: some because of frank speech suffered beating with the staff, others because of displeasing the ruler met with suspicion—treated all alike, they alike suffer imperial punishment; I fear this harms the kingly way and shows that magnanimity has not been fully extended.
translations.idiomatic: Some were beaten for speaking frankly, others fell under suspicion for displeasing the throne—yet all were punished alike. I fear this harms the kingly way and shows that Your Majesty's magnanimity has not yet been fully shown.

sentences.zh: 」由是玄素等稍得敘用。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xuansu and the others gradually obtained restoration to office.
translations.idiomatic: " As a result Xuansu and the others were gradually restored to office.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was given the additional title of Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was given the additional title Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，代於志寧為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, Jingzong replaced Yu Zhining as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong came to the throne, Jingzong replaced Yu Zhining as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 敬宗嫁女與蠻酋馮盎之子，多納金寶，為有司所劾，左授鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: Jingzong gave his daughter in marriage to the son of the barbarian chieftain Feng Ang and accepted much gold and treasure; he was impeached by the responsible officials and demoted to Prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong married his daughter to the son of the tribal chieftain Feng Ang and accepted a large bride-price in gold and jewels. The authorities impeached him, and he was demoted to prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 永徽三年，入為衛尉卿，加弘文館學士，兼修國史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghui he entered the capital as Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, was given the additional post of academician of the Hongwen Institute, and concurrently compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 3 he returned to the capital as Minister of the Imperial Stud, was made an academician of the Hongwen Institute, and again took charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 六年，復拜禮部尚書，高宗將廢皇后王氏而立武昭儀，敬宗特贊成其計。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was again appointed Minister of Rites. When Gaozong was about to depose Empress Wang and establish Consort Wu Zhaoyi, Jingzong especially supported the plan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was again made Minister of Rites. When Gaozong planned to depose Empress Wang and install Consort Wu, Jingzong strongly backed the scheme.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌、褚遂良、韓瑗等並直言忤旨，敬宗與李義府潛加誣構，並流死於嶺外。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji, Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, and others all spoke frankly against the imperial will; Jingzong and Li Yifu secretly added false charges, and they were all exiled and died beyond the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji, Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, and others spoke out against the plan; Jingzong and Li Yifu secretly fabricated charges against them, and all died in exile beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，加太子賓客，尋冊拜侍中，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing he was given the additional post of Guest of the Crown Prince; soon he was formally appointed Palace Attendant and supervised compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 1 he was made Guest of the Crown Prince; soon afterward he was appointed Palace Attendant and put in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 三年，進封郡公，尋贈其父善心為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year he was advanced to enfeoffment as Duke of a commandery; soon his father Shanzin was posthumously given the post of Prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was enfeoffed as Duke of a commandery; soon afterward his father Shanzin was posthumously named prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗因於古長安城遊覽，問侍臣曰：「朕觀故城舊基，宮室似與百姓雜居，自秦、漢已來，幾代都此？

translations.literal: Gaozong, while touring the old Chang'an city, asked his attendant ministers: "When I look at the old foundations of the former city, the palaces seem to have been mixed with common dwellings. Since Qin and Han, how many dynasties have made this their capital?
translations.idiomatic: While touring the old city of Chang'an, Gaozong asked his ministers: "Looking at these old foundations, the palaces seem to have stood among ordinary houses. Since Qin and Han times, how many dynasties have used this as their capital?

sentences.zh: 」敬宗對曰：「秦都咸陽，郭邑連跨渭水，故云『渭水貫都，以象天河。

translations.literal: " Jingzong replied: "The Qin made their capital at Xianyang; the outer walls and city stretched across the Wei River, hence the saying 'The Wei runs through the capital, like the River of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingzong replied: "The Qin capital was at Xianyang, with the outer walls spanning the Wei River—hence the saying, 'The Wei runs through the capital like the River of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 』至漢惠帝始築此城，其後苻堅、姚萇、後周並都之。

translations.literal: ' It was Emperor Hui of Han who first built this city; afterward Fu Jian, Yao Chang, and the Later Zhou all made it their capital.
translations.idiomatic: ' Emperor Hui of Han was the first to build this city; later Fu Jian, Yao Chang, and the Northern Zhou all made it their capital.

sentences.zh: 」帝又問：「昆明池是漢武帝何年中開鑿？

translations.literal: " The emperor asked again: "In which year of Emperor Wu of Han was Kunming Pool excavated?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then asked: "In which year of Emperor Wu of Han was Kunming Pool dug?

sentences.zh: 」敬宗對曰：「武帝遣使通西南夷，而為昆明滇池所閉，欲伐昆明國，故因鎬之舊澤，以穿此池，用習水戰，元狩三年事也。

translations.literal: " Jingzong replied: "Emperor Wu sent envoys to open relations with the southwestern Yi, but they were blocked by the Kunming people at Dian Pool; wishing to attack the state of Kunming, he therefore used the old marshlands of Hao to cut this pool for practicing naval warfare—it was a matter of the third year of Yuanshuo.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingzong replied: "Emperor Wu sent envoys to the southwestern tribes, but they were blocked at Dianchi by the Kunming people. He wished to attack the state of Kunming, so he used the old marshes near the capital to dig this pool for naval drill—it was in Yuanshuo 3.

sentences.zh: 」帝因令敬宗與弘文館學士具檢秦、漢已來歷代宮室處所以奏。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon ordered Jingzong and the academicians of the Hongwen Institute to compile and report on the sites of palaces of successive dynasties since Qin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then ordered Jingzong and the Hongwen academicians to research and report on the palace sites of every dynasty since Qin and Han.

sentences.zh: 其年，代李義府為中書令，任遇之重，當朝莫比。

translations.literal: That year he replaced Li Yifu as Chief Minister of the Secretariat; the weight of his appointment and favor was unmatched at court.
translations.idiomatic: That year he replaced Li Yifu as Chief Minister of the Secretariat; no one at court enjoyed greater favor.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，從新令改為右相，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, following the new regulations he was changed to Right Chancellor and given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2, under the new administrative code, he became Right Chancellor and was given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 三年，冊拜太子少師、同東西台三品，並依舊監修國史。

translations.literal: In the third year he was formally appointed Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince and Associate of the Third Rank with the Eastern and Western Offices, and as before supervised compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was formally appointed Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince and Third-Rank Associate of both Chancelleries, and continued to supervise the national history as before.

sentences.zh: 乾封初，以敬宗年老，不能行步，特令與司空李勣，每朝日各乘小馬入禁門至內省。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfeng, because Jingzong was old and could not walk, a special order was issued that he and Minister of Works Li Ji should each ride a small horse on court days through the forbidden gate to the inner offices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianfeng era, because Jingzong was too old to walk, a special order allowed him and Minister of Works Li Ji each to ride a pony through the palace gate to the inner offices on court days.

sentences.zh: 敬宗自掌知國史，記事阿曲。

translations.literal: Jingzong himself took charge of the national history and recorded events in a flattering and distorted manner.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jingzong took charge of the national history himself, he recorded events in a flattering and distorted way.

sentences.zh: 初，虞世基與敬宗父善心同為宇文化及所害，封德彝時為內史舍人，備見其事，因謂人曰：「世基被誅，世南匍匐而請代；

translations.literal: Earlier, Yu Shiji and Jingzong's father Shanzin were both killed by Yuwen Huaji; Feng Deyi was then Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat and witnessed the whole affair, and he said to people: "When Shiji was to be executed, Shinan crawled prostrate to beg to die in his place;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yu Shiji and Jingzong's father Shanzin had both been killed by Yuwen Huaji. Feng Deyi, then a drafting secretary, witnessed the whole affair and remarked: "When Shiji was condemned, his brother Shinan crawled forward and begged to die in his place;

sentences.zh: 善心之死，敬宗舞蹈以求生。

translations.literal: when Shanzin was to die, Jingzong danced and capered to save his life."
translations.idiomatic: but when Shanzin was to die, Jingzong danced and capered to save his own life."

sentences.zh: 」人以為口實，敬宗深銜之，及為德彝立傳，盛加其罪惡。

translations.literal: " People took this as a byword; Jingzong deeply resented it, and when he wrote a biography for Deyi he greatly exaggerated his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: " People repeated this story against him. Jingzong deeply resented it, and when he wrote Deyi's biography he greatly exaggerated his faults.

sentences.zh: 敬宗嫁女與左監門大將軍錢九隴，本皇家隸人，敬宗貪財與婚，乃為九隴曲敘門閥，妄加功績，並升與劉文靜、長孫順德同卷。

translations.literal: Jingzong gave his daughter in marriage to Qian Jiulong, General of the Left Gate Guards, who was originally a bondservant of the imperial house; Jingzong, greedy for wealth, entered the marriage alliance and therefore distorted Jiulong's lineage, falsely added achievements, and placed him in the same fascicle as Liu Wenjing and Zhangsun Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: He married his daughter to Qian Jiulong, General of the Left Gate Guards, who had originally been an imperial bondservant. Greedy for the bride-price, Jingzong falsified Jiulong's pedigree, invented achievements for him, and placed his biography in the same volume as those of Liu Wenjing and Zhangsun Shunde.

sentences.zh: 敬宗為子娶尉遲寶琳孫女為妻，多得賂遺，及作寶琳父敬德傳，悉為隱諸過咎。

translations.literal: Jingzong had his son marry the granddaughter of Yuchi Baolin and received many bribes; when he wrote the biography of Baolin's father Jingde, he concealed all his faults.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged for his son to marry the granddaughter of Yuchi Baolin and accepted many bribes. When he wrote the biography of Baolin's father Jingde, he concealed every fault.

sentences.zh: 太宗作《威鳳賦》以賜長孫無忌，敬宗改雲賜敬德。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong composed the "Ode to the Majestic Phoenix" to bestow on Zhangsun Wuji; Jingzong altered it to say it was bestowed on Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had written the "Ode to the Majestic Phoenix" as a gift to Zhangsun Wuji; Jingzong changed the record to say it had been given to Jingde.

sentences.zh: 白州人龐孝泰，蠻酋凡品，率兵從征高麗，賊知其懦，襲破之。

translations.literal: Pang Xiaotai of Baizhou was a barbarian chieftain of ordinary rank who led troops on the campaign against Goguryeo; the enemy knew he was cowardly and attacked and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xiaotai of Baizhou was a tribal chieftain of no distinction who led troops against Goguryeo. The enemy knew he was timid, attacked him, and destroyed his force.

sentences.zh: 敬宗又納其寶貨，稱孝泰頻破賊徒，斬獲數萬。

translations.literal: Jingzong again accepted his treasures and goods and claimed that Xiaotai repeatedly defeated the enemy bands and beheaded or captured tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong took bribes from him and recorded that Xiaotai had repeatedly routed the enemy and killed or captured tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 漢將驍健者，唯蘇定方與龐孝泰耳，曹繼叔、劉伯英皆出其下。

translations.literal: Among valiant Han generals, only Su Dingfang and Pang Xiaotai, while Cao Jishu and Liu Boying were all beneath them.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote that among valiant Han generals only Su Dingfang and Pang Xiaotai stood out, with Cao Jishu and Liu Boying beneath them.

sentences.zh: 虛美隱惡如此！

translations.literal: Thus did he invent praise and conceal wrongdoing!
translations.idiomatic: Such was the way he invented praise and concealed wrongdoing!

sentences.zh: 初，高祖、太宗兩朝實錄，其敬播所修者，頗多詳直，敬宗又輒以己愛憎曲事刪改，論者尤之。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Veritable Records of the Gaozu and Taizong reigns that Xu Jingbo had compiled, much was detailed and straightforward; Jingzong again repeatedly altered and deleted matters according to his likes and dislikes, and critics especially blamed him for this.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records of the Gaozu and Taizong reigns compiled by Xu Jingbo had been detailed and straightforward; Jingzong repeatedly altered and deleted passages according to his personal likes and dislikes, which critics especially condemned.

sentences.zh: 然自貞觀已來，朝廷所修《五代史》及《晉書》、《東殿新書》、《西域圖志》、《文思博要》、《文館詞林》、《累璧》、《瑤山玉彩》《姓氏錄》、《新禮》，皆總知其事，前後賞賚，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Yet from Zhenguan onward, in such court compilations as the History of the Five Dynasties, the Book of Jin, the New Books of the Eastern Hall, the Gazetteer of the Western Regions, the Literary Essence Compendium, the Forest of Literary Phrases, the Accumulated Jade Tablets, the Jade Mountain Splendor, the Register of Surnames, and the New Rites—all were under his overall direction, and the rewards bestowed on him before and after are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the Zhenguan era onward he oversaw such major court compilations as the History of the Five Dynasties, the Book of Jin, the New Books of the Eastern Hall, the Gazetteer of the Western Regions, the Literary Essence Compendium, the Forest of Literary Phrases, the Accumulated Jade Tablets, the Jade Mountain Splendor, the Register of Surnames, and the New Rites, and the rewards he received are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 敬宗好色無度。

translations.literal: Jingzong was licentious beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong was licentious beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 其長子昂頗有才藻，歷位太子舍人。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ang was quite gifted in literary talent and served as Attendant of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ang was gifted in letters and served as Attendant of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 母裴氏早卒。

translations.literal: His mother, the Pei clan, died early.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's mother, of the Pei clan, had died young.

sentences.zh: 裴侍婢有姿色，敬宗嬖之，以為繼室，假姓虞氏。

translations.literal: A maid of the Pei household was beautiful; Jingzong favored her and made her his successor wife, giving her the false surname Yu.
translations.idiomatic: A maid of the Pei household was beautiful; Jingzong favored her, took her as his new wife, and gave her the false surname Yu.

sentences.zh: 昂素與通，烝之不絕，敬宗怒黜虞氏，加昂以不孝，奏請流於嶺外。

translations.literal: Ang had long been intimate with her and continued the liaison without cease; Jingzong in anger dismissed the Yu woman, charged Ang with unfilial conduct, and memorialized requesting his exile beyond the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: Ang had long been intimate with her and the affair continued. Jingzong in anger dismissed the Yu woman, charged Ang with unfilial conduct, and memorialized to have him exiled beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，表乞昂還，除虔化令，尋卒。

translations.literal: During Xianqing he submitted a memorial begging that Ang be returned; Ang was appointed magistrate of Qianhua and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianqing he memorialized to have Ang recalled; Ang was appointed magistrate of Qianhua and soon died.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，抗表乞骸骨，詔聽致仕，仍加特進，俸祿如舊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianheng he submitted a memorial resisting [delay] and begging to retire on account of old bones; an edict permitted him to leave office, and he was still given the special advancement rank, with salary as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianheng 1 he submitted a memorial asking to retire; the emperor granted his request, gave him the special advancement rank, and kept his salary unchanged.

sentences.zh: 三年薨，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the third year he died; he was eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died, at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 高宗為之舉哀，廢朝三日，詔文武百官就第赴哭，冊贈開府儀同三司、揚州大都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: Gaozong mourned him, suspended court for three days, and ordered civil and military officials to go to his residence to wail; by patent he was posthumously given Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Bells and Grand Protector General of Yangzhou, and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong mourned him, suspended court for three days, and ordered all officials to attend the mourning at his residence. He was posthumously given the titles Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Bells and Grand Protector General of Yangzhou, and was buried with honor at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 文集八十捲。

translations.literal: His collected writings ran to eighty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to eighty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 太常將定謚，博士袁思古議曰：「敬宗位以才升，歷居清級，然棄長子於荒徼，嫁少女於夷落。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices was about to fix his posthumous name; Erudite Yuan Sigu proposed: "Jingzong rose in rank through talent and held high clear offices, yet he abandoned his eldest son in the wild frontier and married his young daughter to a barbarian settlement.
translations.idiomatic: When the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was about to fix his posthumous name, Erudite Yuan Sigu proposed: "Jingzong rose through talent and held high office, yet he abandoned his eldest son in the frontier wilds and married his young daughter to a barbarian chief.

sentences.zh: 聞《詩》學《禮》，事絕於趨庭；

translations.literal: To hear the Odes and study the Rites—such things ended at the courtyard gate;
translations.idiomatic: He never taught his son the Odes and Rites in the family courtyard;

sentences.zh: 納采問名，唯聞於黷貨。

translations.literal: betrothal gifts and inquiry of the name were heard of only in connection with corrupt wealth.
translations.idiomatic: betrothal and marriage were known only through bribes.

sentences.zh: 白圭斯玷，有累清塵，易名之典，須憑實行。

translations.literal: A white jade tablet thus stained blemishes pure repute; the canon for changing the name must rely on actual conduct.
translations.idiomatic: A white jade tablet is stained—his reputation is tarnished. The canon for posthumous names must rest on actual conduct.

sentences.zh: 按謚法『名與實爽曰繆』，請謚為『繆』。

translations.literal: According to the canon of posthumous names, 'when name and reality diverge it is called Miu [False],' and I request the posthumous name 'Miu.'"
translations.idiomatic: By the canon of posthumous names, 'when name and reality diverge, the name is Miu [False].' I request the posthumous name Miu."

sentences.zh: 」敬宗孫、太子舍人彥伯不勝其恥，與思古大相忿競，又稱思古與許氏先有嫌隙，請改謚官。

translations.literal: " Jingzong's grandson, Attendant of the Crown Prince Yanbo, unable to bear the shame, quarreled fiercely with Sigu and also claimed that Sigu had earlier had a grudge against the Xu clan, requesting that the posthumous-name officer be changed.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingzong's grandson Yanbo, Attendant of the Crown Prince, could not bear the shame and quarreled fiercely with Sigu, claiming that Sigu had long held a grudge against the Xu family and asking that another officer be assigned to fix the name.

sentences.zh: 太常博士王福畤議曰：「謚者，飾終之稱也，得失一朝，榮辱千載。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wang Fuchou proposed: "The posthumous name is the title that adorns the end; gain or loss in a single morning, honor or shame for a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Wang Fuchou of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices proposed: "The posthumous name adorns a man's end: a moment's judgment, a reputation for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 若使嫌隙是實，即合據法推繩；

translations.literal: If the grudge is real, then by law he should be prosecuted;
translations.idiomatic: If the grudge is real, he should be prosecuted by law;

sentences.zh: 如其不虧直道，義不可奪，官不可侵。

translations.literal: if he has not violated the straight path, righteousness cannot be taken from him, and his office cannot be encroached upon.
translations.idiomatic: but if he has not violated the straight path, his judgment cannot be set aside and his office cannot be taken from him.

sentences.zh: 二三其德，何以言禮？

translations.literal: To be of two or three minds in virtue—how can one speak of ritual?
translations.idiomatic: To change one's principles—how can one speak of ritual propriety?

sentences.zh: 福畤忝當官守，匪躬之故。

translations.literal: Fuchou, unworthy in holding his official charge, acts for the sake of not betraying his person.
translations.idiomatic: I hold this office unworthily, but I must not betray my duty.

sentences.zh: 若順風阿意，背直從曲，更是甲令虛設，將謂禮院無人，何以激揚雅道，顧視同列！

translations.literal: If one follows the wind and flatters intent, turning from the straight to the crooked, this would make the statutes an empty form and show the Ritual Office to have no men—how then to rouse the refined way and face one's colleagues!
translations.idiomatic: If I bow to pressure and abandon the straight path for the crooked, the statutes become empty words and the Ritual Office is shown to have no integrity. How then can we uphold the refined way or face our colleagues?

sentences.zh: 請依思古謚議為定。

translations.literal: I request that Sigu's proposal for the posthumous name be adopted as final.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Sigu's proposal be adopted as final.

sentences.zh: 」戶部尚書戴至德謂福畤曰：「高陽公任遇如此，何以定謚為『繆』？

translations.literal: " Minister of Revenue Dai Zhide said to Fuchou: "The Duke of Gaoyang enjoyed such appointment and favor—how can you fix his posthumous name as 'Miu'?
translations.idiomatic: " Minister of Revenue Dai Zhide said to Fuchou: "The Duke of Gaoyang enjoyed such favor at court—how can you fix his posthumous name as Miu?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「昔晉司空何曾薨，太常博士秦秀謚為繆丑公。

translations.literal: " He replied: "In olden times when He Zeng, Minister of Works of Jin, died, Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Qin Xiu gave him the posthumous name Duke Miu-Chou [False and Ugly].
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "When He Zeng, Minister of Works of Jin, died, Erudite Qin Xiu gave him the posthumous name Duke Miu-Chou [False and Ugly].

sentences.zh: 何曾既忠且孝，徒以日食萬錢，所以貶為繆丑。

translations.literal: He Zeng was both loyal and filial, yet solely because he spent ten thousand cash a day on food, he was therefore demoted to Miu-Chou.
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng was loyal and filial, yet solely because he spent ten thousand cash a day on food, he was given the name Miu-Chou.

sentences.zh: 況敬宗忠孝不逮於曾，飲食男女之累，有逾於何氏，而謚之為『繆』，無負於許氏矣。

translations.literal: How much more so Jingzong, whose loyalty and filial piety did not reach He Zeng's, and whose burdens of food, drink, and women exceeded the He's—yet to give him the posthumous name 'Miu' does the Xu clan no wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong's loyalty and filial piety did not equal He Zeng's, and his indulgence in food, drink, and women exceeded He Zeng's—yet to give him the name Miu does the Xu family no injustice.

sentences.zh: 」時有詔令尚書省五品已上重議，禮部尚書袁思敬議稱：「按謚法『既過能改曰恭』，請謚曰『恭』。

translations.literal: " At the time an edict ordered officials of the fifth rank and above in the Secretariat to deliberate again; Minister of Rites Yuan Sijing proposed: "According to the canon of posthumous names, 'having faults yet able to reform is called Gong [Respectful],' and I request the posthumous name 'Gong.'"
translations.idiomatic: " An edict then ordered officials of the fifth rank and above in the Secretariat to deliberate again. Minister of Rites Yuan Sijing proposed: "By the canon, 'having faults yet able to reform is called Gong [Respectful].' I request the posthumous name Gong."

sentences.zh: 」詔從其議。

translations.literal: " An edict followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict followed his proposal.

sentences.zh: 彥伯，昂之子，起家著作郎。

translations.literal: Yanbo was the son of Ang; he began his career as Gentleman of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was Ang's son; he began his career as Gentleman of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 敬宗末年文筆，多令彥伯代作。

translations.literal: In Jingzong's later years, much of his literary writing was entrusted to Yanbo to compose in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingzong's later years Yanbo ghost-wrote most of his compositions.

sentences.zh: 又納婢妾讒言，奏流於嶺表，後遇赦得還，除太子舍人。

translations.literal: He also fell victim to slander by maidservants and concubines, was memorialized for exile beyond the mountain passes, and later returned on a general pardon and was appointed Attendant of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Maidservants and concubines slandered him, and he was exiled beyond the passes. After a general amnesty he returned and was appointed Attendant of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 早卒，有集十捲。

translations.literal: He died young; his collected writings ran to ten fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He died young, leaving collected writings of ten fascicles.

sentences.zh: 李義府

translations.literal: Li Yifu
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu

sentences.zh: 李義府，瀛州饒陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Yifu was a native of Raoyang in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu came from Raoyang in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 其祖為梓州射洪縣丞，因家於永泰。

translations.literal: His grandfather served as Assistant Magistrate of Shehong county in Zizhou, and the family settled in Yongtai.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather had served as assistant magistrate of Shehong in Zizhou, and the family made its home in Yongtai.

sentences.zh: 貞觀八年，劍南道巡察大使李大亮以義府善屬文，表薦之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenguan, Li Daliang, Inspector of the Jiannan Circuit, because Yifu was skilled at literary composition submitted a memorial recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 8 Li Daliang, inspector of the Jiannan circuit, recommended Yifu to the throne for his skill in writing.

sentences.zh: 對策擢第，補門下省典儀。

translations.literal: In the policy-response examination he ranked at the top and was appointed Master of Ceremonial Forms in the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He placed at the top in the policy-response examination and was appointed master of ceremonial forms in the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎劉洎、侍書御史馬周皆稱薦之，尋除監察御史。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Chancellery Liu Ji and Palace Censor Ma Zhou both praised and recommended him, and soon he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Liu Ji and Palace Censor Ma Zhou both recommended him, and he was soon appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 又敕義府以本官兼侍晉王。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered Yifu, while retaining his current post, to serve concurrently as attendant to Prince Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered Yifu to serve Prince Jin concurrently while keeping his existing post.

sentences.zh: 及升春宮，除太子舍人，加崇賢館直學士，與太子司議郎來濟俱以文翰見知，時稱來、李。

translations.literal: When the prince entered the Eastern Palace, Yifu was appointed Attendant of the Crown Prince and added as Resident Academician of the Chongxian Hall; he and Secretary for Discussion of the Crown Prince Lai Ji were both recognized for their literary talents, and at the time they were called Lai and Li.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince entered the Eastern Palace, Yifu became Attendant of the Crown Prince and resident academician of the Chongxian Hall. He and Lai Ji, secretary for discussion of the crown prince, were both known for their writing, and people spoke of them as Lai and Li.

sentences.zh: 義府嘗獻《承華箴》，其辭曰：

translations.literal: Yifu once presented the "Chenghua Zhen" (Admonition for the Heir Apparent); its text reads:
translations.idiomatic: Yifu once submitted the Chenghua Zhen (Admonition for the Heir Apparent), which reads:

sentences.zh: 邃初冥昧，元氣氤氳。

translations.literal: In the deep beginning, darkness and obscurity; primordial qi swirled in dense mist.
translations.idiomatic: At the first beginning all was dark and formless, and primordial breath gathered in swirling mist.

sentences.zh: 二儀始闡，三才既分。

translations.literal: The Two Powers began to unfold; the Three Origins were already divided.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth opened forth, and the three realms took their separate forms.

sentences.zh: 司乾立宰，出《震》為君。

translations.literal: Heaven established the ruler; from the hexagram Zhen came the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven set the ruler in place, and from the hexagram Zhen the sovereign arose.

sentences.zh: 化昭淳樸，道映典墳。

translations.literal: Transformations illumined simplicity and plainness; the Way was reflected in the canonical texts.
translations.idiomatic: Civilization revealed plain virtue, and the Way shone forth in the classic books.

sentences.zh: 功成揖讓，事極華、勳。

translations.literal: Merit achieved through yielding; affairs reached the fullness of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Merit was completed through yielding, and rule reached the height of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 肇興夏啟，降及姬文。

translations.literal: The rise began with Xia Qi, descending to Ji Wen.
translations.idiomatic: It began with the rise of Xia Qi and descended to King Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 咸資繼德，永樹高芬。

translations.literal: All relied on inherited virtue; forever they planted lofty fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: All drew on inherited virtue and planted an enduring noble renown.

sentences.zh: 百代沿襲，千齡奉聖。

translations.literal: For a hundred generations they followed in succession; for a thousand ages they honored the sage.
translations.idiomatic: For a hundred generations the tradition continued, and for a thousand years the sage was honored.

sentences.zh: 粵若我後，丕承寶命。

translations.literal: As for our sovereign, he greatly inherits the precious mandate.
translations.idiomatic: As for our sovereign, he grandly receives the precious mandate.

sentences.zh: 允穆三階，爰齊七政。

translations.literal: Truly harmonizing the three tiers, he aligns with the seven regulators.
translations.idiomatic: He harmonizes the three ranks of rule and brings the seven celestial powers into alignment.

sentences.zh: 時雍化洽，風移俗盛。

translations.literal: When harmony prevailed, civilization was complete; the wind shifted and customs flourished.
translations.idiomatic: In an age of harmony, civilization flourished, customs changed, and society prospered.

sentences.zh: 載崇國本，式延家慶。

translations.literal: He upholds the foundation of the state and extends family fortune.
translations.idiomatic: He exalts the foundation of the state and extends the blessings of the royal house.

sentences.zh: 《震》維標德，《離》警體正。

translations.literal: The hexagram Zhen marks virtue; Li warns of upright conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen marks the standard of virtue; Li warns one to keep the person upright.

sentences.zh: 寄切宗祧，事隆監撫。

translations.literal: Entrusted with ancestral rites; affairs weighty in supervision and nurture.
translations.idiomatic: He is entrusted with the ancestral line, and his charge in overseeing and nurturing the heir is great.

sentences.zh: 思皇茂則，敬詢端輔。

translations.literal: Reflect on splendid norms; reverently consult upright assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Reflect on noble standards and reverently seek counsel from upright ministers.

sentences.zh: 業光啟、誦，藝優干羽。

translations.literal: His achievements shine like Qi and Song; his arts surpass the shield-and-feather dance.
translations.idiomatic: His accomplishments shine like those of Qi and Song, and his attainments surpass the great peace dance.

sentences.zh: 九載崇儒，三朝問豎，歷選儲儀，遺文在斯。

translations.literal: For nine years he honored Confucian learning; across three reigns he was questioned while still a youth; having passed through selection of the heir's rites, the written legacy is here.
translations.idiomatic: For nine years he honored Confucian learning; across three reigns he was tested while still young; he has passed through the rites of heir selection, and the written legacy remains here.

sentences.zh: 望試登俎，高諭喬枝。

translations.literal: He aspires to trial on the sacrificial stand; lofty instruction comes from the tall branch.
translations.idiomatic: He looks to be tested at the sacrificial stand and to receive lofty instruction from the high branch of the royal tree.

sentences.zh: 俯容思順，非禮無施。

translations.literal: Bow in humility and seek accord; nothing unritual is done.
translations.idiomatic: Bow humbly, seek harmony, and do nothing contrary to ritual.

sentences.zh: 前修盛業，來哲通規。

translations.literal: The great achievements of former worthies; the universal norms bequeathed by later sages.
translations.idiomatic: The great achievements of earlier exemplars and the universal standards left by later sages.

sentences.zh: 飭躬是蹈，則叡問風馳；

translations.literal: If one disciplines the person and follows this path, then sagely inquiry comes swift as the wind;
translations.idiomatic: If one disciplines oneself and follows this path, sagely counsel will come swift as the wind;

sentences.zh: 立志或爽，則玄猷日虧。

translations.literal: if one's resolve wavers, then profound designs daily diminish.
translations.idiomatic: but if resolve wavers, profound plans will daily decline.

sentences.zh: 無恃尊極，修途難測；

translations.literal: Do not rely on supreme eminence; the cultivated path is hard to measure;
translations.idiomatic: Do not rely on supreme rank; the path of self-cultivation is hard to fathom;

sentences.zh: 無恃親賢，失德靡全。

translations.literal: do not rely on close and worthy kin; losing virtue leaves nothing whole.
translations.idiomatic: do not rely on close and worthy kin—lose virtue, and nothing remains intact.

sentences.zh: 勿輕小善，積小而名自聞；

translations.literal: Do not slight small good; accumulated small goods make one's name known of itself;
translations.idiomatic: Do not slight small acts of goodness; accumulated little by little, they make a name known of themselves;

sentences.zh: 勿輕微行，累微而身自正。

translations.literal: do not slight slight conduct; accumulated slight conduct makes the person upright of itself.
translations.idiomatic: do not slight small acts of conduct; accumulated little by little, they make the person upright of themselves.

sentences.zh: 佞諛有類，邪巧多方。

translations.literal: Flattery has its types; wicked cunning has many methods.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers come in many forms, and devious schemers employ various methods.

sentences.zh: 其萌不絕，其害必彰。

translations.literal: If the sprout is not cut off, the harm must become manifest.
translations.idiomatic: If their roots are not cut off, their harm will surely become evident.

sentences.zh: 監言斯屏，儲業攸昌。

translations.literal: Guard against such words and exclude them; then the heir's cause will flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Guard against such words and banish them, and the heir's enterprise will flourish.

sentences.zh: 竊惟令嗣，有殊前事。

translations.literal: I reflect that this excellent heir differs from prior affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that this excellent heir is unlike cases of the past.

sentences.zh: 雖以貴以賢，而非長非次。

translations.literal: Though noble and worthy, he is neither eldest nor next in order.
translations.idiomatic: Though he is honored and worthy, he is neither the eldest son nor next in line.

sentences.zh: 皇明眷德，超倫作貳。

translations.literal: The emperor's brilliance favors virtue; surpassing the norm, he was made second heir.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's wisdom favors virtue and, transcending ordinary measure, made him crown prince.

sentences.zh: 匪懋聲華，莫酬恩異。

translations.literal: Unless one cultivates brilliant reputation, one cannot requite such extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: Unless one cultivates brilliant reputation and honor, one cannot repay such extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 匪崇徽烈，莫符天志。

translations.literal: Unless one upholds noble virtue and achievements, one cannot accord with Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Unless one upholds noble virtue and great deeds, one cannot accord with Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 勉之又勉，光茲守器。

translations.literal: Strive again and again; let this guardianship of the vessel shine.
translations.idiomatic: Strive again and again, and let this guardianship of the heir's charge shine forth.

sentences.zh: 下臣司箴，敢告近侍。

translations.literal: I, a low minister charged with admonition, dare report to those nearest the throne.
translations.idiomatic: I, a lowly minister charged with admonition, dare convey this to those nearest the throne.

sentences.zh: 太子表上其文，優詔賜帛四十匹，又令預撰《晉書》。

translations.literal: The crown prince submitted a memorial presenting the text; an edict in his favor granted forty bolts of silk, and he was also ordered to participate in compiling the Book of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince submitted the text to the throne; an edict in Yifu's favor granted him forty bolts of silk, and he was ordered to take part in compiling the Book of Jin.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, Yifu was transferred to Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, Yifu was promoted to Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，兼修國史，加弘文館學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui he concurrently compiled the national history and was added as Academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 2 he was assigned to compile the national history and was made an academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 高宗將立武昭儀為皇后，義府嘗密申協贊，尋擢拜中書侍郎、同中書門下三品，監修國史，賜爵廣平縣男。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was about to establish Lady Wu as empress, Yifu once secretly supported and assisted the plan; soon he was promoted and appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, Third-Rank Associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery, supervisor of the national history, and ennobled as Baron of Guangping county.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong was about to make Lady Wu empress, Yifu secretly supported the plan. Soon he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Third-Rank Associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery, placed in charge of the national history, and ennobled as Baron of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 義府貌狀溫恭，與人語必嬉怡微笑，而褊忌陰賊。

translations.literal: Yifu appeared gentle and warm in countenance; whenever he spoke with others he would smile with affability, yet he was narrow-minded, jealous, and covertly treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu looked gentle and courteous; whenever he spoke with anyone he smiled warmly, yet he was narrow-minded, jealous, and secretly treacherous.

sentences.zh: 既處權要，欲人附己，微忤意者，輒加傾陷。

translations.literal: Once he held critical power, he wanted others to attach themselves to him; anyone who slightly crossed him he would destroy through false charges.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held real power he demanded that others attach themselves to him, and anyone who slightly crossed him he would ruin with false charges.

sentences.zh: 故時人言義府笑中有刀，又以其柔而害物，亦謂之「李貓。

translations.literal: Therefore people of the time said Yifu had a blade hidden in his smile, and because he was soft yet harmed others, they also called him "Cat Li."
translations.idiomatic: People of the time said Yifu had a blade hidden in his smile, and because he was soft-spoken yet harmed others, they also called him "Cat Li."

sentences.zh: 」顯慶元年，以本官兼太子右庶子，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Xianqing, while retaining his current post he was additionally appointed Right Attendant of the Crown Prince and advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: " In Xianqing 1 he was additionally appointed Right Attendant of the Crown Prince while retaining his current post, and was advanced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 有洛州婦人淳于氏，坐奸繫於大理，義府聞其姿色，囑大理丞畢正義求為別宅婦，特為雪其罪。

translations.literal: A woman of Luozhou named Chunyu was imprisoned at the Court of Judicial Review on an adultery charge; Yifu, hearing of her beauty, instructed Vice Director Bi Zhengyi to obtain her as a concubine in a separate residence and specially had her crimes cleared.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of Luozhou named Chunyu was imprisoned at the Court of Judicial Review on an adultery charge. Yifu, hearing of her beauty, told Vice Director Bi Zhengyi to obtain her as a concubine in a separate residence and had her crimes cleared.

sentences.zh: 卿段寶玄疑其故，遽以狀聞，詔令按其事，正義惶懼自縊而死。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Duan Baoxuan suspected the circumstances and immediately reported them; an edict ordered an investigation, and Zhengyi in panic hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Duan Baoxuan suspected foul play and immediately reported the matter. An edict ordered an investigation, and Zhengyi in panic hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 侍御史王義方廷奏義府犯狀，因言其初容貌為劉洎、馬周所幸，由此得進，言詞猥褻。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Wang Yifang memorialized at court on Yifu's offenses, adding that in his early years his appearance had won the favor of Liu Ji and Ma Zhou, through which he had advanced—his language was coarse and lewd.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Wang Yifang memorialized at court on Yifu's crimes, adding that in his early years his looks had won the favor of Liu Ji and Ma Zhou, through which he had risen—his language was coarse and indecent.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，出義方為萊州司戶，而不問義府奸濫之罪。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry, sent Yifang out as Revenue Clerk of Laizhou, and did not inquire into Yifu's corrupt misdeeds.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry, sent Yifang out as revenue clerk of Laizhou, and did not investigate Yifu's corrupt misconduct.

sentences.zh: 義府云：「王御史妄相彈奏，得無愧乎？

translations.literal: Yifu said: "Supervising Censor Wang has recklessly memorialized against me—should he not feel ashamed?
translations.idiomatic: Yifu said, "Supervising Censor Wang has recklessly accused me—should he not feel ashamed?

sentences.zh: 」義方對云：「仲尼為魯司寇七日，誅少正卯於兩觀之下；

translations.literal: " Yifang replied: "When Confucius served as Minister of Crime of Lu for seven days, he executed Shaozheng Mao below the two towers of the gate;
translations.idiomatic: " Yifang replied, "When Confucius served as Minister of Crime of Lu for seven days, he executed Shaozheng Mao below the two gate towers;

sentences.zh: 義方任御史旬有六日，不能去奸邪於雙闕之前，實以為愧。

translations.literal: I have served as censor for sixteen days and could not remove a wicked official before the twin gates—I truly feel ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: I have served as censor for sixteen days and could not remove a wicked official before the palace gates—I truly am ashamed.

sentences.zh: 」尋兼太子左庶子。

translations.literal: " Soon afterward he was additionally appointed Left Attendant of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was additionally appointed Left Attendant of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 二年，代崔敦禮為中書令，兼檢校御史大夫，監修國史、學士並如故。

translations.literal: In the second year he replaced Cui Dunli as Chief Minister of the Secretariat, concurrently serving as Inspector General of the Censorate; his posts as supervisor of the national history and academician remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he replaced Cui Dunli as Chief Minister of the Secretariat and concurrently served as Inspector General of the Censorate; his duties supervising the national history and his academician post remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子賓客，進封河間郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Guest of the Crown Prince and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Hejian commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally appointed Guest of the Crown Prince and was enfeoffed as Duke of Hejian commandery.

sentences.zh: 三年，又追贈其父德晟為魏州刺史，諸子孩抱者並列清官，詔為造甲第，榮寵莫之能比。

translations.literal: In the third year his late father Desheng was posthumously given Prefect of Weizhou; even his infant sons were all listed in clear offices; an edict ordered construction of a grand mansion for him—honor and favor none could match.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year his late father Desheng was posthumously made Prefect of Weizhou; even his infant sons were given prestigious offices; an edict ordered a grand mansion built for him—no one could match such honor and favor.

sentences.zh: 而義府貪冒無厭，與母、妻及諸子、女婿賣官鬻獄，其門如市。

translations.literal: But Yifu was insatiably greedy; with his mother, wife, sons, and sons-in-law he sold offices and sold judgments, and his gate was like a market.
translations.idiomatic: But Yifu was insatiably greedy; with his mother, wife, sons, and sons-in-law he sold offices and sold judgments, and his gate was like a marketplace.

sentences.zh: 多引腹心，廣樹朋黨，傾動朝野。

translations.literal: He brought in many trusted men, widely planted factional ties, and shook court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: He brought in many trusted followers, built a wide network of factions, and shook both court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 初，杜正倫為中書侍郎，義府時任典儀，至是乃與正倫同為中書令。

translations.literal: Initially Du Zhenglun had been Vice Director of the Secretariat while Yifu held the post of Master of Ceremonial Forms; now they both served as Chief Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Du Zhenglun had been Vice Director of the Secretariat while Yifu was master of ceremonial forms; now they both served as Chief Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 正倫每以先進自處，不下義府，而中書侍郎李友益密與正倫共圖議義府，更相伺察。

translations.literal: Zhenglun always placed himself as the senior and would not defer to Yifu; Vice Director Li Youyi secretly joined Zhenglun in plotting against Yifu, each side watching the other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun always treated himself as the senior and would not defer to Yifu, while Vice Director Li Youyi secretly joined Zhenglun in plotting against Yifu, each side watching the other.

sentences.zh: 義府知而密令人封奏其事。

translations.literal: Yifu learned of this and secretly had someone submit a sealed memorial reporting the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu learned of this and secretly had someone submit a sealed memorial reporting it.

sentences.zh: 正倫與義府訟於上前，各有曲直。

translations.literal: Zhenglun and Yifu argued their case before the emperor; each had right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun and Yifu argued their case before the emperor, each presenting his own grievances.

sentences.zh: 上以大臣不和，兩責之，左貶義府為普州刺史，正倫為橫州刺史，友益配流峰州。

translations.literal: Because the senior ministers were not in harmony, the emperor blamed both; Yifu was demoted to Prefect of Puzhou, Zhenglun to Prefect of Hengzhou, and Youyi was sentenced to penal exile in Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because the senior ministers were at odds, the emperor blamed both men: Yifu was demoted to prefect of Puzhou, Zhenglun to prefect of Hengzhou, and Youyi was sentenced to penal exile in Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，復召義府兼吏部尚書、同中書門下三品，自余官封如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Yifu was again recalled as Minister of the Civil Office concurrent with Third-Rank Associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery; his other offices and enfeoffment remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Yifu was recalled as Minister of the Civil Office and Third-Rank Associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery; his other offices and titles remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 龍朔元年，丁母憂去職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longshuo he left office upon mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 1 he left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 二年，起復為司列太常伯、同東西台三品。

translations.literal: In the second year he was recalled from mourning as Director of the Ministry of Rites for Officials and Third-Rank Associate of the Eastern and Western Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was recalled from mourning as Director of the Ministry of Rites for Officials and Third-Rank Associate of the Eastern and Western Departments.

sentences.zh: 義府尋請改葬其祖父，營墓於永康陵側。

translations.literal: Yifu soon requested to reinter his grandfather and built a tomb beside Yongkang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu soon requested to reinter his grandfather and built a tomb beside Yongkang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 三原令李孝節私課丁夫車牛，為其載土築墳，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: Magistrate Li Xiaojie of Sanyuan privately levied corvée laborers and ox-carts to haul earth and build the mound for him, day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Li Xiaojie of Sanyuan privately levied corvée laborers and ox-carts to haul earth and build the mound for him, working day and night without rest.

sentences.zh: 於是高陵、櫟陽、富平、雲陽、華原、同官、涇陽等七縣，以孝節之故，懼不得已，悉課丁車赴役。

translations.literal: Thereupon seven counties—Gaoling, Liyang, Fuping, Yunyang, Huayuan, Tongguan, and Jingyang—because of Xiaojie, fearing they had no choice, all levied laborers and carts for the service.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon seven counties—Gaoling, Liyang, Fuping, Yunyang, Huayuan, Tongguan, and Jingyang—fearing they had no choice because of Xiaojie, all levied laborers and carts for the work.

sentences.zh: 高陵令張敬業恭勤怯懦，不堪其勞，死於作所。

translations.literal: Magistrate Zhang Jingye of Gaoling was respectful, diligent, timid, and weak; he could not endure the labor and died at the worksite.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Zhang Jingye of Gaoling was dutiful but timid and weak; he could not endure the labor and died at the worksite.

sentences.zh: 王公已下，爭致贈遺，其羽儀、導從、轜輶、器服，並窮極奢侈。

translations.literal: From princes and dukes downward all vied to send gifts; escorts, attendants, carriages, and regalia were all pushed to the utmost luxury.
translations.idiomatic: From princes and dukes downward all vied to send gifts; escorts, attendants, carriages, and regalia were all pushed to the utmost extravagance.

sentences.zh: 又會葬車馬祖奠供帳，自灞橋屬於三原，七十里間，相繼不絕。

translations.literal: At the joint funeral as well, funeral carriages, preliminary offerings, and canopies from Ba Bridge to Sanyuan, seventy li in all, continued without break.
translations.idiomatic: At the joint funeral as well, the line of funeral carriages, preliminary offerings, and canopies from Ba Bridge to Sanyuan stretched seventy li without interruption.

sentences.zh: 武德已來，王公葬送之盛，未始有也。

translations.literal: Since Wude, no prince or duke's funeral procession had ever reached such splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wude era no prince or duke's funeral procession had ever reached such splendor.

sentences.zh: 義府本無藻鑑才，怙武後之勢，專以賣官為事。

translations.literal: Yifu originally had no talent for discerning men; relying on Empress Wu's power, he devoted himself solely to selling offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu had no real talent for judging men; relying on Empress Wu's power, he devoted himself solely to selling offices.

sentences.zh: 銓序失次，人多怨讟。

translations.literal: Rank and order in appointments were disordered, and many people complained and cursed.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments were made out of proper order, and many people complained and cursed.

sentences.zh: 時殷王初出閣，又以義府兼王府長史。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Yin had just left the palace; Yifu was again appointed concurrent Chief Administrator of the princely household.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Prince of Yin had just left the palace, and Yifu was again appointed concurrent chief administrator of the princely household.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷右相，殷王府長史仍知選事並如故。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Right Chancellor; his posts as Chief Administrator of the Prince of Yin's household and controller of appointments remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Right Chancellor; his posts as chief administrator of the Prince of Yin's household and controller of appointments remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 義府入則諂言自媚，出則肆其奸宄，百僚畏之，無敢言其過者。

translations.literal: Yifu would flatter and ingratiate himself within the palace and outside would indulge his wicked schemes; the hundred officials feared him, and none dared speak of his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the palace Yifu flattered and ingratiated himself; outside he indulged his wicked schemes. The officials feared him, and none dared speak of his faults.

sentences.zh: 帝頗知其罪失，從容誡義府云：「聞卿兒子、女婿皆不謹慎，多作罪過，我亦為卿掩覆，未即公言，卿可誡勖，勿令如此。

translations.literal: The emperor was quite aware of his crimes and faults; calmly he admonished Yifu: "I hear your sons and sons-in-law are all careless and commit many offenses. I have covered this for you and have not yet spoken openly; you should warn and instruct them—do not let them go on this way.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was quite aware of his misconduct. Calmly he admonished Yifu: "I hear your sons and sons-in-law are all careless and commit many offenses. I have covered this for you and have not yet spoken openly. You should warn and instruct them—do not let them go on this way.

sentences.zh: 」義府勃然變色，腮頸俱起，徐曰：「誰向陛下道此？

translations.literal: " Yifu suddenly changed color in anger, his cheeks and neck swelling, and slowly said: "Who told Your Majesty this?
translations.idiomatic: " Yifu suddenly flushed with anger, his cheeks and neck swelling, and slowly said, "Who told Your Majesty this?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「但我言如是，何須問我所從得耶！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "But I speak thus—why must you ask where I learned it!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "But I speak as I do—why must you ask where I learned it!

sentences.zh: 」義府睆然，殊不引咎，緩步而去。

translations.literal: " Yifu looked blank, showed no sign of accepting blame, and walked away at an unhurried pace.
translations.idiomatic: " Yifu looked blank, showed no sign of accepting blame, and walked away at an unhurried pace.

sentences.zh: 上亦優容之。

translations.literal: The emperor also treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also treated him with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 初，五禮儀注，自前代相沿，吉凶畢舉。

translations.literal: Initially the annotated regulations on the five rites had been handed down from previous generations, with both auspicious and inauspicious rites fully set forth.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the annotated regulations on the five rites had been handed down from previous generations, with both auspicious and inauspicious rites fully recorded.

sentences.zh: 太常博士蕭楚材、孔志約以皇室凶禮為預備凶事，非臣子所宜言之。

translations.literal: Erudites Xiao Chucai and Kong Zhiyue of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices held that inauspicious rites for the imperial house, as preparations for inauspicious events, were not what subjects should speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites Xiao Chucai and Kong Zhiyue of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices held that inauspicious rites for the imperial house, as preparations for imperial mourning, were not what subjects should discuss.

sentences.zh: 義府深然之。

translations.literal: Yifu deeply agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是悉刪而焚焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon all were deleted and burned.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all of them were deleted and burned.

sentences.zh: 義府既貴之後，又自言本出趙郡，始與諸李敘昭穆，而無賴之徒苟合，藉其權勢，拜伏為兄叔者甚眾。

translations.literal: After Yifu had risen to eminence, he also declared that his origins were from Zhao commandery and began with the various Lis to arrange senior and junior in the clan genealogy; riffraff attached themselves, borrowed his power, and many bowed and acknowledged him as elder brother or uncle.
translations.idiomatic: After Yifu had risen to eminence, he also claimed that his family came from Zhao commandery and began arranging senior and junior rank with the various Li clans. Riffraff attached themselves to him, borrowed his power, and many bowed and acknowledged him as elder brother or uncle.

sentences.zh: 給事中李崇德初亦與同譜敘昭穆，及義府出為普州刺史，遂即除削。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Li Chongde had at first also arranged senior and junior rank together in the same genealogy; when Yifu went out to serve as prefect of Pu, he was immediately removed and stricken.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Li Chongde had at first also joined Yifu in arranging senior and junior rank in the clan genealogy. When Yifu was sent out as prefect of Pu, Chongde was promptly struck from the roll.

sentences.zh: 義府聞而銜之，及重為宰相，乃令人誣構其罪，竟下獄自殺。

translations.literal: Yifu heard of this and harbored resentment; when he again became chief minister, he had someone falsely construct charges against him, and in the end he was thrown into prison and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu heard of it and nursed a grudge. Once he had regained the chancellorship, he had men fabricate charges against Chongde, who was eventually thrown into prison and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 初，貞觀中，太宗命吏部尚書高士廉、御史大夫韋挺、中書侍郎岑文本、禮部侍郎令狐德棻等及四方士大夫諳練門閥者修《氏族志》，勒成百卷，升降去取，時稱允當，頒下諸州，藏為永式。

translations.literal: Initially, in the Zhenguan era, Emperor Taizong ordered Minister of Personnel Gao Shilian, Censor-in-Chief Wei Ting, Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wenben, Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen, and others, together with scholar-officials from all quarters versed in eminent clans, to compile the Genealogy Records of Clans; when completed it ran to a hundred scrolls. Its promotions, demotions, inclusions, and exclusions were at the time called fair; it was distributed to all prefectures and stored as a permanent model.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era, Emperor Taizong ordered Gao Shilian as Minister of Personnel, Wei Ting as Censor-in-Chief, Cen Wenben as Vice Director of the Secretariat, Linghu Defen as Vice Minister of Rites, and other scholar-officials from across the realm who knew the eminent clans to compile the Genealogy Records of Clans. The finished work ran to a hundred scrolls; its rankings were widely judged fair, issued to every prefecture, and preserved as a permanent standard.

sentences.zh: 義府恥其家代無名，乃奏改此書，專委禮部郎中孔志約、著作郎楊仁卿、太子洗馬史玄道、太常丞呂才重修。

translations.literal: Yifu was shamed that his family through the generations had no fame; he therefore memorialized to alter this book and specially entrusted Erudite of Rites Kong Zhiyue, Drafting Secretary Yang Renqing, Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household Shi Xuandao, and Assistant Director of Imperial Sacrifices Lü Cai to revise it anew.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed that his line had never ranked among the great families, Yifu memorialized to revise the work and put Kong Zhiyue of the Ministry of Rites, Drafting Secretary Yang Renqing, Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household Shi Xuandao, and Assistant Director of Imperial Sacrifices Lü Cai in charge of a wholesale rewrite.

sentences.zh: 志約等遂立格云：「皇朝得五品官者，皆升士流。

translations.literal: Zhiyue and the others then established criteria saying: "In Our Dynasty whoever obtains a fifth-rank office shall all be promoted into the scholar-official stream.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyue and the others then set a rule: "In Our Dynasty, anyone who holds a fifth-rank office shall be entered among the gentry.

sentences.zh: 」於是兵卒以軍功致五品者，盡入書限，更名為《姓氏錄》。

translations.literal: " Thereupon soldiers and common troops who through military achievement attained fifth rank all entered the limits of the book; it was renamed Records of Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon common soldiers promoted to fifth rank through military merit were all entered in the register, and the work was retitled Records of Surnames.

sentences.zh: 由是搢紳士大夫多恥被甄敘，皆號此書為「勳格」。

translations.literal: Because of this the gentry and scholar-officials were mostly ashamed to be selected and catalogued; all called this book the "Meritorious Register."
translations.idiomatic: Many gentry officials were ashamed to be listed in it and dubbed the book the "Meritorious Register."

sentences.zh: 義府仍奏收天下《氏族志》本焚之。

translations.literal: Yifu still memorialized to collect copies of the Genealogy Records of Clans throughout the realm and burn them.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu also memorialized to collect every copy of the Genealogy Records of Clans in the empire and burn them.

sentences.zh: 關東魏、齊舊姓，雖皆淪替，猶相矜尚，自為婚姻。

translations.literal: The old surnames of Wei and Qi in the lands east of the Pass, though all fallen and displaced, still honored one another and formed marriages only among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The old Wei and Qi clans east of the Pass, though fallen from power, still looked down on others and intermarried only among themselves.

sentences.zh: 義府為子求婚不得，乃奏隴西李等七家，不得相與為婚。

translations.literal: Yifu sought marriage for his son but could not obtain it; he therefore memorialized that the seven families including the Longxi Li must not marry one another.
translations.idiomatic: When Yifu failed to secure a marriage for his son among those families, he memorialized that seven families including the Longxi Li were forbidden to intermarry with one another.

sentences.zh: 陰陽占候人杜元紀為義府望氣，雲「所居宅有獄氣，發積錢二千萬乃可厭勝。

translations.literal: Du Yuanji, a man of yin-yang divination and astrological observation, read the aura of qi for Yifu and said, "Your residence has prison qi; only by spending twenty million in accumulated cash can it be counteracted and overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yuanji, a practitioner of yin-yang lore and divination, examined the cosmic signs over Yifu's house and declared, "There is an aura of imprisonment over your residence. You must spend twenty million cash from your hoard to dispel it.

sentences.zh: 」義府信之，聚斂更急切。

translations.literal: " Yifu believed this and gathered and exacted money all the more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: " Yifu believed him and squeezed money from others more ruthlessly than ever.

sentences.zh: 義府居母服，有制朔望給哭假，義府輒微服與元紀凌晨共出城東，登古冢候望，哀禮都廢。

translations.literal: While Yifu was observing mourning for his mother, regulations on the new and full moons granted leave for weeping; Yifu repeatedly in plain dress went out with Yuanji at daybreak from the eastern gate of the city, climbed ancient tombs to observe and watch, and mourning rites were wholly abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother, Yifu was entitled by regulation to leave on the new and full moons for weeping. Instead he repeatedly slipped out before dawn in plain dress with Yuanji, climbed ancient tombs east of the city to scan the heavens, and abandoned mourning ritual entirely.

sentences.zh: 由是人皆言其窺覘災眚，陰懷異圖。

translations.literal: Thereupon everyone said that he was spying out calamities and secretly harbored a rebellious design.
translations.idiomatic: People began to say he was watching for omens of disaster and secretly plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 義府又遣其子右司議郎津，召長孫無忌之孫延，謂曰：「相為得一官，數日詔書當出。

translations.literal: Yifu also sent his son Jin, Right Secretariat Discussant, to summon Yan, grandson of Zhangsun Wuji, and said to him, "I shall get you an office; in a few days the edict will be issued.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu also sent his son Jin, Right Secretariat discussant, to summon Yan, grandson of Zhangsun Wuji, and told him, "I will get you a post; the edict should come out in a few days.

sentences.zh: 」居五日，果授延司津監，乃取延錢七百貫。

translations.literal: " After five days, Yan was indeed appointed Superintendent of the River Pass; Jin then took seven hundred strings of cash from Yan.
translations.idiomatic: " Five days later Yan was indeed appointed river pass superintendent, and Jin took seven hundred strings of cash from him.

sentences.zh: 於是右金吾倉曹參軍楊行穎表言義府罪狀，制下司刑太常伯劉祥道與侍御詳刑對推其事，仍令司空李勣監焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yang Xingying, Military Assistant in the Right Jinwu Granary Office, memorialized stating Yifu's crimes; an edict was issued directing Vice Minister of Justice Liu Xiangdao together with investigating censors to examine the case in detail, and the Minister of Works Li Ji was also ordered to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: Then Yang Xingying, a military assistant in the Right Jinwu granary office, memorialized listing Yifu's offenses. An edict ordered Vice Minister of Justice Liu Xiangdao and investigating censors to examine the charges, with Minister of Works Li Ji supervising the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 按皆有實，乃下制曰：「右相、行殷王府長史、河間郡公李義府，洩禁中之語，鬻寵授之朝恩；

translations.literal: Upon investigation everything was found to be true; thereupon an edict was issued saying: "Right Counselor, Acting Chief Administrator of the Prince of Yin's household, Duke of Hejian commandery Li Yifu leaked words from within the forbidden precinct, sold favor and granted the court's grace for profit;
translations.idiomatic: The investigation confirmed every charge, and an edict was issued: "Right Counselor Li Yifu, Duke of Hejian, acting chief administrator of the Prince of Yin's household, leaked palace secrets and sold imperial favor for profit;

sentences.zh: 交占候之人，輕朔望之哀禮。

translations.literal: He associated with diviners and observers of omens and treated lightly the mourning rites due on the new and full moons.
translations.idiomatic: He consorted with diviners and scorned the mourning obligations owed on the new and full moons.

sentences.zh: 蓄邪黷貨，實玷衣冠；

translations.literal: He hoarded wickedness and amassed corrupt wealth, truly staining the robes of office;
translations.idiomatic: He hoarded ill-gotten wealth and disgraced the robe of office;

sentences.zh: 稔惡嫉賢，載虧政道。

translations.literal: Long steeped in evil and jealous of the worthy, he repeatedly harmed the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: Long steeped in villainy and jealous of the worthy, he repeatedly corrupted public life.

sentences.zh: 特以任使多年，未忍便加重罰，宜從遐棄，以肅朝倫。

translations.literal: Only because he had been employed for many years, I could not bear immediately to impose a heavier punishment; it is fitting that he be sent to distant banishment to restore order in the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Only because he had served many years could I not bring myself to punish him more severely at once; he should be banished to the far borderlands to restore discipline at court.

sentences.zh: 可除名長流巂州。

translations.literal: He may be stripped of his name and permanently banished to Xi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Let his name be struck from the rolls and let him be permanently exiled to Xi prefecture.
