sentences.zh: 其子太子右司議郎津，專恃權門，罕懷忌憚，姦淫是務，賄賂無厭，交遊非所，潛報機密，亦宜明罰，屏跡荒裔。

translations.literal: His son Jin, Right Assistant Censor of the Heir Apparent, relied exclusively on his powerful house, rarely harbored fear, made lechery his business, was insatiable in bribes, consorted with improper persons, and secretly reported confidential matters; he too should receive clear punishment and be banished to the wild frontier.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin, Right Assistant Censor to the Heir Apparent, traded on his family's power without restraint, gave himself to debauchery, took bribes without end, kept disreputable company, and leaked secrets; he too deserves open punishment and exile to the wilderness.

sentences.zh: 可除名長流振州。

translations.literal: He may be stripped of his name and permanently banished to Zhen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Let his name be struck from the rolls and let him be permanently exiled to Zhen prefecture.

sentences.zh: 」義府次子率府長史洽、千牛備身洋、子婿少府主簿柳元貞等，皆憑恃受贓，併除名長流延州。

translations.literal: " Yifu's second son Qia, Chief of the Palace Guard Office, Yang, Palace Guard, son-in-law Minor Treasury Clerk Liu Yuanzhen, and others all relied on their positions to accept bribes; together they were stripped of their names and permanently banished to Yan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Yifu's second son Qia, chief of the palace guard office, Yang of the palace guard staff, and his son-in-law Liu Yuanzhen, minor treasury clerk—all had traded on their connections to take bribes and were likewise stripped of rank and permanently exiled to Yan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朝野莫不稱慶，時人為之語曰：「今日巨唐年，還誅四凶族。

translations.literal: Through court and countryside none failed to rejoice; people of the time made a saying for it: "Today in the great Tang's year, the four evil clans are again executed.
translations.idiomatic: The court and the country rejoiced as one, and people at the time said: "In this great age of Tang we have cut down the four evil clans once again.

sentences.zh: 」四凶者，謂洽及柳元貞等四人也。

translations.literal: " The four evils meant Qia, Liu Yuanzhen, and the others—four persons in all.
translations.idiomatic: " The "four evils" meant Qia, Liu Yuanzhen, and two others—four men in all.

sentences.zh: 或作《河間道行軍元帥劉祥道破銅山大賊李義府露布》，榜之通衢。

translations.literal: Someone composed A Battle Report of Liu Xiangdao, Campaign Marshal of the Hejian Circuit, on His Defeat of the Great Bandit Li Yifu of Copper Mountain and posted it in the public thoroughfares.
translations.idiomatic: Someone wrote a victory proclamation entitled "Campaign Marshal Liu Xiangdao of the Hejian Circuit Defeats the Great Bandit Li Yifu of Copper Mountain" and posted it in the main streets.

sentences.zh: 義府先多取人奴婢，及敗，一時奔散，各歸其家。

translations.literal: Yifu had earlier taken many people's slaves and servants; when he fell, at once they fled and scattered, each returning to their homes.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu had previously seized many people's slaves and servants; when he fell, they fled at once and returned to their own homes.

sentences.zh: 《露布》稱「混奴婢而亂放，各識家而競入」者，謂此也。

translations.literal: Where the Battle Report says "mixing slave girls and servants and releasing them in disorder, each knowing their home and rushing to enter" refers to this.
translations.idiomatic: The proclamation's line about "releasing servants and slave girls in wild confusion, each recognizing his home and racing to get back in" referred to this.

sentences.zh: 乾封元年，大赦，長流人不許還，義府憂憤發疾卒，年五十餘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianfeng, at a great amnesty, persons permanently banished were not permitted to return; Yifu, worried and angry, fell ill and died, aged over fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In 666, at a general amnesty, those in permanent exile were not allowed to return. Yifu, gripped by worry and rage, sickened and died in his fifties.

sentences.zh: 文集三十捲，傳於代；

translations.literal: A collected works of thirty scrolls was transmitted to the age;
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in thirty scrolls that circulated in later ages;

sentences.zh: 又著《宦遊記》二十捲，尋亡失。

translations.literal: He also wrote Records of Official Travel in twenty scrolls, which soon was lost.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Records of Official Travel in twenty scrolls, but that work was soon lost.

sentences.zh: 自義府流放後，朝士常憂懼，恐其復來，及聞其死，於是始安。

translations.literal: From the time Yifu was exiled, court officials constantly worried and feared that he would return; when they heard of his death, only then did they grow calm.
translations.idiomatic: After Yifu's exile, court officials lived in constant fear that he might return; only when news of his death arrived did they breathe easily.

sentences.zh: 少子湛

translations.literal: The Younger Son Zhan
translations.idiomatic: The Younger Son Zhan

sentences.zh: 義府少子湛，年六歲時，以父貴授周王文學。

translations.literal: Yifu's younger son Zhan, when six years old, because of his father's eminence was appointed Literary Master to the Prince of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu's youngest son Zhan was only six when his father's rank won him appointment as literary master to the Prince of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，累遷右散騎常侍，襲封河間郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he was promoted in successive steps to Right Regular Attendant, and inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Hejian commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Shenlong reign he rose through successive posts to Right Regular Attendant and inherited the dukedom of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 時鳳閣侍郎張柬之將誅張易之兄弟，遂引湛為左羽林將軍，令與敬暉等啟請皇太子，備陳將誅易之兄弟意，太子許之。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director of the Fengge Secretariat Zhang Jianzhi was about to execute the Zhang Yizhi brothers; he therefore brought in Zhan as General of the Left Feathered Forest Guard and ordered him together with Jing Hui and others to request an audience with the Heir Apparent, fully stating their intention to execute the Yizhi brothers; the Heir Apparent agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Director Zhang Jianzhi of the Fengge Secretariat prepared to kill the Zhang Yizhi brothers, he brought Zhan in as general of the Left Feathered Forest Guard and had him join Jing Hui and the others in asking audience with the crown prince. They laid out their plan to kill the Yizhi brothers, and the prince agreed.

sentences.zh: 及兵發，湛與右羽林大將軍李多祚等詣東宮迎皇太子，拒而不時出，湛進啟曰：「逆豎反道亂常，將圖不軌，宗社危敗，實在須臾。

translations.literal: When the troops set out, Zhan together with General of the Right Feathered Forest Guard Li Duozuo and others went to the Eastern Palace to welcome the Heir Apparent; he refused and for a time did not come out. Zhan stepped forward and reported: "These rebellious villains oppose the Way and disorder the constant order, about to plot improper conduct; the altars of state face peril and ruin—the need is truly in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: When the troops moved, Zhan went with General Li Duozuo of the Right Feathered Forest Guard and others to the Eastern Palace to fetch the crown prince. The prince refused and lingered indoors. Zhan stepped forward and said, "These traitorous villains have overturned the natural order and mean to rebel. The realm hangs by a thread.

sentences.zh: 湛等諸將與南衙執事剋期誅翦，伏願殿下暫至玄武門，以副眾望。

translations.literal: We generals together with the officeholders of the Southern Yamen have set a date to cut them down; I humbly hope Your Highness will for the moment come to the Xuanwu Gate to satisfy the hopes of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The generals and the officials of the Southern Yamen have fixed a date to cut them down. I beg Your Highness to come at once to the Xuanwu Gate and answer the army's expectation.

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「凶豎悖亂，誠合誅夷，然聖躬不豫，慮有驚動。

translations.literal: " The Heir Apparent said: "These vicious villains are perverse and rebellious; truly they ought to be executed and exterminated, yet Our Sage Person is unwell, and I fear there will be alarm and disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince said, "Those villains deserve death, but the emperor is ill, and I fear the shock would harm him.

sentences.zh: 公等且止，以俟後圖。

translations.literal: You gentlemen stop for now and wait for a later plan.
translations.idiomatic: Stop for now and wait for a better moment.

sentences.zh: 」湛曰：「諸將棄家族，共宰相同心戮力，匡輔社稷，殿下奈何不哀其懇誠而欲陷之鼎鑊？

translations.literal: " Zhan said: "The generals have abandoned their families to join the chief ministers in one heart and combined strength to support and restore the altars of state—how can Your Highness not pity their earnest sincerity and instead wish to plunge them into the boiling cauldron?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhan said, "These generals have abandoned their families to stand with the chief ministers and save the throne. How can Your Highness ignore their earnest plea and send them to the cauldron instead?

sentences.zh: 湛等微命，雖不足惜，殿下速出自止遏。

translations.literal: Our petty lives, though not worth cherishing—Your Highness, quickly come out yourself to stop and restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Our lives are nothing—but Your Highness must come out now and take command.

sentences.zh: 」太子乃馳馬就路。

translations.literal: " The Heir Apparent then galloped forth on the road.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince then spurred his horse and rode out.

sentences.zh: 湛從至玄武門，斬關而入，率所部兵直至則天所寢長生殿，環繞侍衛。

translations.literal: Zhan followed to the Xuanwu Gate, cut through the gate and entered, and led the troops under his command straight to the Hall of Eternal Life where Wu Zetian slept, encircling her in protective guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan followed him to the Xuanwu Gate, broke through the barrier, and led his troops straight to the Hall of Eternal Life where Empress Wu slept, forming a ring of guards around her.

sentences.zh: 因奏：「臣等奉令誅逆賊易之、昌宗，恐有漏洩，遂不獲預奏，輒陳兵禁掖，是臣等死罪。

translations.literal: He then reported: "We your subjects, having received the order to execute the rebellious bandits Yizhi and Changzong, feared there might be a leak; therefore we could not first report it and rashly deployed troops within the forbidden quarters—this is capital crime for us your subjects.
translations.idiomatic: He then reported, "We received orders to execute the traitors Yizhi and Changzong. Fearing a leak, we could not report in advance and have rashly brought troops into the inner palace—this is a capital offense for us.

sentences.zh: 」則天謂湛曰：「卿亦是誅易之軍將耶？

translations.literal: " Wu Zetian said to Zhan: "Are you also one of the generals executing Yizhi?
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Wu said to Zhan, "So you too command the troops sent to kill Yizhi?

sentences.zh: 我於汝父子恩不少，何至是也！

translations.literal: I have shown no little favor to you father and son—how can it have come to this!
translations.idiomatic: I have done much for you and your father—how did it come to this!

sentences.zh: 」則天移就上陽宮，因留湛宿衛。

translations.literal: " Wu Zetian moved up to the Shangyang Palace, and thereupon kept Zhan on night watch.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Wu moved to the Shangyang Palace and kept Zhan as her night guard.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，拜右羽林大將軍，進封趙國公，加實封通前滿五百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, he was appointed General of the Right Feathered Forest Guard, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Zhao state, with added substantive fiefs reaching five hundred households in total including previous grants.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong came to the throne, Zhan was made general of the Right Feathered Forest Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao with total income fiefs of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復授左散騎常侍，累轉左領軍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed Left Regular Attendant and in successive transfers became General of the Left Court Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again named Left Regular Attendant and later rose to general of the Left Court Guard.

sentences.zh: 開元初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Kaiyuan reign.

sentences.zh: 崔義玄別有傳。

translations.literal: Cui Yixuan has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yixuan is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰

translations.literal: The Historiographer Comments
translations.idiomatic: The Historiographer Comments

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：許高陽武德之際，已為文皇入館之賓，垂三十年，位不過列曹尹；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Xu of Gaoyang, in the Wude era, was already a guest entering the palace library for the Literary Emperor; for nearly thirty years his rank went no higher than department director;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Xu of Gaoyang entered Emperor Taizong's palace library as a companion as early as the Wude era, yet for nearly thirty years rose no higher than a department director;

sentences.zh: 而馬周、劉洎起羈旅徒步，六七年間，皆登宰執。

translations.literal: yet Ma Zhou and Liu Ji rose from wanderers on foot; within six or seven years both ascended to chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: yet Ma Zhou and Liu Ji, men who had arrived on foot with nothing, reached the chancellorship within six or seven years.

sentences.zh: 考其行實，則高陽之文學宏奧，周、洎無以過之，然而太宗任遇相殊者，良以高陽才優而行薄故也。

translations.literal: Examining their conduct in fact, Gaoyang's literary learning was vast and abstruse—Zhou and Ji could not surpass him; yet the reason Emperor Taizong's employment and favor differed so greatly was truly because Gaoyang's talent was superior but his conduct was thin.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by their deeds, Gaoyang's literary attainments exceeded anything Zhou or Ji could match; yet the reason Taizong favored them so differently was simply that Gaoyang's talent was great but his character was small.

sentences.zh: 及屬嗣君沖暗，嬖妾奸邪，阿附豺狼，窺圖權軸，人之凶險，一至於斯。

translations.literal: When it fell to a succeeding ruler who was dull and dark, with favorite concubines and wicked minions, he fawned upon wolves and jackals and schemed for the hub of power; that a man's viciousness and peril could reach this point—
translations.idiomatic: Under a dull successor surrounded by favored women and wicked flatterers, he fawned on wolves and jackals and schemed for the heart of power. That human depravity could go so far—

sentences.zh: 仲尼所謂「雖有周公之才，不足觀也。

translations.literal: What Confucius called "Even though one have the talent of the Duke of Zhou, he is not worth observing.
translations.idiomatic: This is what Confucius meant when he said, "Even if one had the talent of the Duke of Zhou, he would not be worth watching.

sentences.zh: 」義府才思精密，所謂「猩猩能言」，鄙哉！

translations.literal: " Yifu's talent and thought were precise and subtle—what is called "an orangutan can speak"—how base!
translations.idiomatic: " Yifu was clever and polished—precisely the sort of wit Confucius dismissed when he said, "Even an orangutan can talk"—contemptible!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：貞觀文士，高陽、河間。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Literary men of the Zhenguan era—Gaoyang and Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: In summary: Among Zhenguan's men of letters were Gaoyang and Hejian.

sentences.zh: 圖形學館，染翰書山。

translations.literal: Their likenesses drawn in the Academy, their brushes dipped in the mountain of books.
translations.idiomatic: Their portraits hung in the Academy; their brushes steeped in the mountain of books.

sentences.zh: 進身以筆，得位由奸。

translations.literal: They advanced themselves by the pen and obtained rank through treachery.
translations.idiomatic: They rose by the pen and won office through treachery.

sentences.zh: 為虎傅翼，即又胡顏。

translations.literal: Giving wings to a tiger, they yet had the face to show themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Having given wings to a tiger, they still had the shamelessness to show their faces.
